**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 80, verses 11–17:**

[(p-٦٠٦٠)] Discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[11–17] ﴿Nay, indeed it is a reminder﴾ ﴿so whoever wills may remember it﴾ ﴿in honored scrolls﴾ ﴿exalted and purified﴾ ﴿by the hands of scribes﴾ ﴿noble and dutiful﴾ ﴿Woe to man, how ungrateful he is!﴾

His saying, glorified is He, "Nay" is a rebuke against the one who was reproached for it and against repeating the like of it. Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The Prophet ﷺ, after that, would honor him." Narrated by Abu Ya'la. His saying, exalted is He, "indeed it is a reminder," means that the reproach mentioned is an admonition that must be taken to heart and acted upon according to its requirement.

Al-Shihab said: That his reproach for what was mentioned is an admonition, because even with the greatness of his status and rank with Allah, when he was reproached for the like of it, then what about others? He permitted the pronoun to refer to the verses, to the surah, to the command of equality among people, and to the call of Islam. His saying, exalted is He, "so whoever wills may remember it," means: whoever wills may preserve it, taking it as from (dhikr) meaning the opposite of forgetting; or he may be admonished by it, from (al-tadhkir).

Al-Zamakhshari said: He used the masculine pronoun because tadhkirah has the meaning of dhikr and wa'z (admonition). It has also been said: the pronoun refers to the Qur'an, and the speech is a digression.

﴿in honored scrolls﴾ means the scrolls of the verses of the revelation and its surahs.

﴿exalted﴾ means of high standing, ﴿purified﴾ from alteration, deficiency and error.

﴿by the hands of scribes﴾: the plural of safir (safir, a go-between) with the meaning of safir (envoy). Or it is one who went between his people to make peace and reconciliation. It is said: safara bayna al-qawm (he acted as go-between among the people) when he reconciled them, and from it is his saying:

*And I do not abandon mediation between my people, and I do not walk with deceit if I walk.*

As for al-safarah (the scribes), they are either the angels, because they carry the revelation between Allah, exalted is He, and His messengers, as if it were carried in their hands; or the prophets, because they are intermediaries in the revelation, conveying it to people.

﴿noble﴾ means with Him, exalted is He, because of their being chosen for the message. ﴿dutiful﴾ means righteous, the plural of (barr), who is the doer of goodness and benefit.

﴿Woe to man, how ungrateful he is!﴾ Al-Razi said: Know that when He, exalted is He, began by mentioning the story which includes the haughtiness of the chieftains of Quraysh over the poor Muslims, He made His believing servants marvel at that. It is as if it was said: What is the cause of this marvel and haughtiness, when its beginning is a filthy drop and its end is a stinking carcass, and between the two times it carries filth? Therefore, He, exalted is He, mentioned what may serve as a remedy for their marvel and what may serve as a remedy for their disbelief; for the creation of man may be used as evidence for the existence of the Creator and for the affirmation of resurrection, gathering and raising. Its implication is that by "man" is meant the one who is self-sufficient without the noble Qur'an, whose sublime attributes are mentioned, which necessitate turning to it and believing in it. It is also permitted that by "man" is meant the species, encompassing the self-sufficient one and his like among its individuals, not by considering all of its individuals.

Subtleties:

The first: Al-Zamakhshari said: ﴿Woe to man﴾ is a curse upon him, and it is among the most abominable of their curses, because death is the utmost of the hardships and horrors of this world.

The second: Ibn Jarir said: In His saying ﴿how ungrateful he is!﴾ there are two aspects. One of them is the wonder at his disbelief despite Allah's kindness toward him and His favors upon him. The other is "what is it that made him ungrateful?", meaning: what thing made him ungrateful? According to the second, the hamzah (interrogative) is for clarification, as in (aghadda al-ba'eer), (the camel became swollen).

The third: Al-Zamakhshari said regarding this verse: You will not see a style more severe than it, nor more coarse in its body, nor more indicative of wrath, nor more far-reaching in blame, together with the closeness of its two ends, nor more comprehensive for the rebukes, despite the shortness of its body. Its secret is what al-Razi indicated: that His saying ﴿Woe to man﴾ is an alert that they deserved the greatest kinds of punishment, and His saying ﴿how ungrateful he is!﴾ is an alert that they possessed the greatest kinds of ugly and abominable traits.

[(p-٦٠٦٢)] The fourth: In (al-Kashf) it is stated that the curse is not in its literal sense, due to its impossibility from Him, exalted is He, because its origin is incapacity. Therefore, what is meant by it is the expression of wrath considering its first part, and intense blame considering its second part; that is, because the wonder in its well-known meaning is also impossible.
